title: Oddness of the majority function
statement: For every $m\in\mathbb N$, let $M_m$ be the majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, with value $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are false and $-1$ otherwise. For every $x\in\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, complementing every coordinate negates its value: $M_m(\lnot x)=-M_m(x)$.
replaced:
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
Then $M_m(-x)=-M_m(x)$ for every $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, where $-x$ negates every coordinate.
